capture.final_message:
Use the finite/infinite dichotomy for `Cardinal.toNat` as the central mechanism.

Establish these facts independently:

- For finite `α`, `Cardinal.toNat (Cardinal.mk α) = Fintype.card α`.
- For infinite `α`, `Cardinal.toNat (Cardinal.mk α) = 0`.
- A type has cardinality (or finite cardinality) `1` exactly when it is nonempty and subsingleton.

The only subtlety in the `toNat = 1` characterization is excluding infinite types, since `toNat` collapses every infinite cardinal to `0`. Thus `toNat (mk α) = 1` forces finiteness, after which the usual `Fintype.card_eq_one` characterization applies.

Consequently, all four universally quantified propositions in the theorem are true outright. Each displayed `Iff` can therefore be organized by proving its two sides independently from the facts above, rather than trying to derive one substantive cardinal theorem from the other.
